record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: Can entropy-reduction results for correlated repeated actuation by an external feedback controller be applied or extended to derive bounds for other performance measures of feedback-controlled systems, specifically including the maximum attainable flux and the maximum attainable power?

evidence.quote: the entropy reduction of a system due to the correlated repeated actuation of an external controller has been computed

Another open question is the application or the extension of the results found in [13] to find bounds for other performance measures of feedback controlled systems, for example, the maximum attainable flux or power.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic feedback-controlled physical system (for instance, a Langevin or Markov-jump system) on which an external controller acts repeatedly in a temporally correlated manner. The controller measures the state of the system and applies a control protocol at successive times; let p_n(x) denote the joint distribution of system and controller states at cycle n, and define the entropy reduction per cycle

ΔS_red = S(p_{n}) − S(p_{n+1}^{post-control})

attributable to the correlated repeated actuation of the controller. Assume known results that express ΔS_red in terms of the mutual information (or transfer entropy) between system and controller across cycles, providing an upper bound on entropy reduction per cycle.

Let J denote a steady-state thermodynamic flux of interest (e.g. probability current, particle current, or heat current) and let P denote the average power output (rate of useful work extraction) of the feedback-controlled system in its periodic stationary regime.

Problem: Derive, from (or as an extension of) the information-theoretic identities and inequalities that bound the per-cycle entropy reduction ΔS_red under correlated repeated feedback actuation, explicit upper bounds for:

(a) the maximum attainable flux J_max, and
(b) the maximum attainable power P_max,

expressed in terms of information-theoretic quantities (mutual information, transfer entropy, or KL divergences between system+controller distributions) and the physical parameters of the system (temperatures, control period, dissipation).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (including a 2025 preprint on entropic balance with feedback control and ongoing work on information thermodynamics of feedback ratchets) continues to develop information-theoretic inequalities for feedback-controlled systems, but no general result deriving sharp bounds on the maximum attainable flux and power directly from correlated-repeated-actuation entropy-reduction identities appears to have been established. The question remains an active open problem.
